back: A fundamental property of matter. Two kinds exist: positive and negative. Like charges repel, unlike charges attract.
Glass rod rubbed with silk = positive. Plastic rod rubbed with fur = negative.
q = ne, where n is an integer and e = 1.602 x 10^-19 C (elementary charge).
Total charge of an isolated system is always conserved. Charge can be transferred but not created or destroyed.
Conductors: charges free to move (metals, human body). Insulators: charges not free to move (glass, rubber, plastic).
F = k|q1*q2|/r^2, where k = 1/(4*pi*epsilon_0) approx 9 x 10^9 Nm^2C^-2.
F_21 = (1/4*pi*epsilon_0)(q1*q2/r^2_21) * r_hat_21. Force along line joining charges.

front: Value of permittivity of free space (epsilon_0)

back: Force on any charge = vector sum of individual forces due to all other charges. Individual forces are unaffected by presence of others.
E = lim(q->0) F/q. Force per unit positive test charge at a point. Independent of test charge.

front: Electric field due to point charge
back: E = (1/4*pi*epsilon_0)(q/r^2). Radially outward for +q, inward for -q.

front: Force on charge in electric field
back: F = qE. A charge q in field E experiences force qE.

front: Properties of electric field lines (4 rules)
back: (1) Start at + charges, end at - charges. (2) Continuous, no breaks. (3) Never cross. (4) No closed loops in electrostatics.
dPhi = E . dS = E*dS*cos(theta). Units: Nm^2C^-1 or V.m.
p = q x 2a. Vector from -q to +q with magnitude = charge times separation.
E = (1/4*pi*epsilon_0)(2p/r^3). Falls off as 1/r^3.

front: Dipole field on equatorial plane (r >> a)
back: E = -(1/4*pi*epsilon_0)(p/r^3). Half the axial magnitude, opposite direction.

front: Torque on dipole in uniform field
back: tau = p x E. Aligns dipole with field. Zero when p is parallel to E.
sigma = dQ/dS. Charge per unit area. Units: C/m^2.
lambda = dQ/dl. Charge per unit length. Units: C/m.
rho = dQ/dV. Charge per unit volume. Units: C/m^3.
Closed surface integral of E.dA = q_enclosed/epsilon_0. Total flux through closed surface = enclosed charge / epsilon_0.

front: E due to infinite wire (linear density lambda)
back: E = lambda/(2*pi*epsilon_0*r). Radial, falls as 1/r.

front: E due to infinite plane sheet (surface density sigma)
back: E = sigma/(2*epsilon_0). Uniform, independent of distance.

front: E inside and outside a charged spherical shell
back: Outside (r > R): E = q/(4*pi*epsilon_0*r^2) (as if charge at centre). Inside (r < R): E = 0.
1 C is the charge that, placed 1 m from another identical charge in vacuum, experiences a force of 9 x 10^9 N.

front: Ratio of electric to gravitational force (e-p)
back: F_e/F_G approx 10^39. Electric forces are enormously stronger than gravitational forces.
